chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: He narrated to me Ali ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Wassaq, from whom he mentioned, from Al-Khashti, from Abu al-Samit, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays.

He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Mu'alla! If a servant worships Allah for a hundred years between the Rukn and the Maqam, fasting by day and standing in prayer by night, until his eyebrows fall over his eyes and his collarbones meet, becoming a complete old man, yet he is ignorant of our rights, there is no reward for him.'

key_terms.الرُّکْنُ وَالْمَقَامُ: The Rukn and Maqam, specific pillars in the Kaaba associated with Prophet Ibrahim, often used to denote the place of prayer.
key_terms.ثَوَابٌ: Reward, specifically the spiritual reward for acts of worship.
key_terms.حَقِّنَا: Our rights, referring specifically to the rights of the Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt.
key_terms.هَرَماً: A complete old man, indicating advanced age and longevity.

ai.seo_question: Why is knowing the rights of the Imams more important than long-term prayer and fasting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) illustrates that even a century of rigorous devotion in the Sacred Mosque yields no reward if the worshipper lacks gnosis (ma'rifah) of the Ahl al-Bayt's rights, a concept central to Shia theology where Wilayah is the soul of worship. This hadith from *Thawab al-Amal* underscores the distinction between mere ritualistic practice and spiritually valid acts, emphasizing that recognition of the Imam is the prerequisite for the acceptance of all deeds.
